title: How do we expand (a + b) times (a squared + 2ab + b squared)?
description: A bracket of two terms multiplies a bracket of three terms. The six pieces are written, like terms are added, and the result is checked with eigh as one and b as two. Keeko doubts that only first with first and last with last are needed.
teaching_notes: One idea: every term of one bracket multiplies every term of the other, then like terms are added. Watch for students who multiply only first with first and last with last.

source: Expand (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) and check with a = 1, b = 2.
video_script.why: The child has expanded a bracket with three terms by one term. Here a bracket of two terms multiplies a bracket of three terms.
video_script.substitution: Distribute the first bracket over the three terms, write the six pieces, add the like terms, and check with small numbers.
video_script.anchor: eigh plus b multiplying the bracket eigh squared plus two eigh b plus b squared
video_script.wrong_answer: the answer is eigh cubed plus b cubed
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies only first with first and last with last, and says the answer is eigh cubed plus b cubed. With eigh as one and b as two, the question gives twenty seven, but that answer gives only nine.
video_script.payoff_line: Every term multiplies every term, and like terms are added

final_answer.spoken: eigh cubed, plus three eigh squared b, plus three eigh b squared, plus b cubed

never_show: an answer of a cubed plus b cubed, marked as right
maths_rules: a × a² = a³, b × a² = a²b, a × 2ab = 2a²b, b × 2ab = 2ab², a × b² = ab², b × b² = b³
a³ + b³ at a = 1, b = 2 is 9, not 27
video_script.design: One idea: every term multiplies every term, then like terms are added. Assumes the distributive property over three terms. Wrong idea: first with first and last with last are enough. The six pieces stay on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='expr'/>Eigh plus b multiplies the bracket eigh squared plus two eigh b plus b squared.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we multiply this out? How can we check the answer with eigh as one and b as two?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: arrows from a and from b to each of the three terms of the second bracket, making 6 pieces; beside it, a²b and 2a²b lit with the words like terms = same letter numbers

marks.six: arrows run from each of the two terms to each of the three terms, making six pieces

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Each of the two terms in the first bracket multiplies each of the three terms in the second.
That makes six pieces.
<bookmark mark='like'/>Pieces with the same letter numbers are called like terms, and they can be added.

marks.given: the expression (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh plus b times the bracket eigh squared plus two eigh b plus b squared.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expansion, checked with a = 1, b = 2

marks.find: the expansion and the check are written as the things to find

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to expand it and check with eigh as one and b as two.

beats.on_screen: (a + b)a² + (a + b) × 2ab + (a + b)b², by the distributive property

marks.three: the three groups light up one by one

beats.colours: each group in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, use the distributive property over the three terms of the second bracket.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Eigh plus b multiplies eigh squared, then two eigh b, then b squared.

beats.on_screen: a × a² = a³, b × a² = a²b; a × 2ab = 2a²b, b × 2ab = 2ab²; a × b² = ab², b × b² = b³; so a³ + a²b + 2a²b + 2ab² + ab² + b³

marks.p1: a × a² = a³ and b × a² = a²b are written
marks.p3: a × b² = ab² and b × b² = b³ are written
marks.all: a³ + a²b + 2a²b + 2ab² + ab² + b³ is written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>Step two, write the six pieces. Eigh times eigh squared is eigh cubed.
B times eigh squared is eigh squared b.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Eigh times two eigh b is two eigh squared b. B times two eigh b is two eigh b squared.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Eigh times b squared is eigh b squared. B times b squared is b cubed.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Written in a row, the six pieces are all there.

beats.colours: each pair of like terms in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, add the like terms. Eigh squared b and two eigh squared b make three eigh squared b.
One plus two is three.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Eigh b squared and two eigh b squared are like terms too.
They make three eigh b squared.

beats.on_screen: check with a = 1, b = 2: (1 + 2)(1 + 4 + 4) = 3 × 9 = 27; the four pieces 1, 6, 12, 8 add to 27

marks.e: the four pieces 1, 6, 12 and 8 are written and add to 27

narration: <bookmark mark='q'/>Step four, check with eigh as one and b as two. The question gives three times nine, which is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='e'/>The four pieces give one, six, twelve and eight.
Their sum is twenty seven, so the two agree.

marks.pay: the words every term multiplies every term, and like terms are added appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Every term multiplies every term, and like terms are added.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The result is eigh cubed, plus three eigh squared b, plus three eigh b squared, plus b cubed.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble shows a³ + b³; beside it 3 × 9 = 27 and 1 + 8 = 9 are compared; the bubble is crossed out

marks.test: 3 × 9 = 27 and 1 + 8 = 9 are written side by side
marks.strike: the bubble is crossed out and the middle terms 3a²b and 3ab² light up

beats.colours: the wrong bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is eigh cubed plus b cubed, from first with first and last with last.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it with eigh as one and b as two. The question gives twenty seven, but that answer gives one plus eight, only nine.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The middle terms are missing, so every term must multiply every term.
